name: The yard outbuildings — a privy behind every house, a stable for the horse-keepers

existence.note: A privy stood behind every town house of 1835 — there was no other arrangement to be had before sewers — and a household that kept a horse stabled it on its own lot. That much is the norm of the period, not a reading of any yard here; WHICH corner, what size and what finish are dealt by rule from the house's own class and age. docs/LIBERTIES.md L353.

rule.privy: every dwelling lot with a yard behind the house and no committed privy
rule.stable: a dwelling lot whose house's class is merchant, keeper or freight, whose house is a tavern, inn, hotel or boarding house, or whose occupation is a teamster's — and that has no committed stable, barn or carriage shed
rule.where: a rear corner, its back 0.75 m inside the rear lot line (off the alley) and 0.75 m in from the side line, at least 0.6 m clear of every committed wall; the corner is chosen by a hash of the lot id and the other is tried when it is taken

wells: None dealt. docs/RESEARCH/wells.md § 4 refuses a well class for the town — July 1835 Chicago drank from the lake by cart — and that ruling stands; data/wells/ draws only the wells a source places.
dwellings_off_plat_note: Dwellings standing on no platted lot have no lot line to put an alley behind; they are counted, not drawn.
